---
title: Build an agent app
description: Copy a host, a web app, or a terminal interface and change it from there
---

## Make an API call

```ts title="host.ts"
import { sqliteStore } from "@nyte-ai/host";
import { chatOnlyProvider } from "@nyte-ai/host/providers";
import { sdk } from "@nyte-ai/sdk";

const store = sqliteStore({ path: "./agent.db" });
const host = await sdk.open({
  store,
  plugins: [{ id: "chat-only", environment: chatOnlyProvider() }],
  workspace: { kind: "chat-only", locator: null },
});

const session = await host.sessions.create({
  configuration: { model: { provider: "openai-codex", id: "{{modelId}}" } },
});
const receipt = await session.send("Hello");
const end = await receipt.settled();
const view = await session.view();

console.log(end.kind, JSON.stringify(view.messages, null, 2));

await host.close();
await store.close();
```

`sdk.open` composes a host in this process and runs its sessions there. `send` admits the message
and returns a receipt: admission, not an answer. `settled()` waits for how the run ended:
`completed`, `stopped` or `failed`. `view()` is one snapshot of what a client draws: `messages`,
`turns`, `execution`, `background` and `changes`. For a live view, use `watch()` as in
[Make a web app](#make-a-web-app). The store is yours, so close it after the host.

The host keeps provider credentials in its store, encrypted with the key in `~/.nyte/secret.key`.
Sign in once per store, before the first send:

```ts title="host.ts"
import process from "node:process";
import { createInterface } from "node:readline/promises";

const catalog = await host.models.list();

if (
  catalog.providers.find((provider) => provider.id === "openai-codex")?.credential === "missing"
) {
  const prompt = createInterface({ input: process.stdin, output: process.stdout });
  const login = host.models.login({ provider: "openai-codex", method: { kind: "oauth" } });

  for await (const step of login.steps()) {
    if (step.kind === "open") console.log("Sign in at", step.url, step.code ?? "");
    if (step.kind === "paste") await login.answer(await prompt.question(`${step.message} `));
    if (step.kind === "failed") throw new Error(step.reason);
  }

  prompt.close();
}
```

`plugins` lists the host's core plugins, with exactly one environment provider per workspace
kind.

To work in a project folder, serve it with the local provider:

```ts title="host.ts"
import { sqliteStore } from "@nyte-ai/host"; // [!code --]
import { chatOnlyProvider } from "@nyte-ai/host/providers"; // [!code --]
import { localProvider, sqliteStore } from "@nyte-ai/host"; // [!code ++]
import process from "node:process"; // [!code ++]

const host = await sdk.open({
  store,
  plugins: [{ id: "chat-only", environment: chatOnlyProvider() }], // [!code --]
  workspace: { kind: "chat-only", locator: null }, // [!code --]
  plugins: [{ id: "local", environment: localProvider() }], // [!code ++]
  workspace: { kind: "local", path: process.cwd() }, // [!code ++]
});
```

There is no trust step. A registered workspace runs, and the folder's own plugins, skills and
instructions load with it: `.nyte/plugins`, `.nyte/skills`, `.agents/skills`, `.nyte/prompts`,
`AGENTS.md` and `CLAUDE.md`. The agent gets unrestricted tools in that folder. It isn't a sandbox,
and Nyte doesn't ask per tool call.

## Make a web app

The SDK packages aren't on npm yet. The install commands below work once they publish under `@next`.

The host needs Node 26.4 or later.

### Vite

Create a React app and install the public SDK packages:

```sh
pnpm create vite chat-web --template react-ts
cd chat-web
pnpm install
pnpm add @nyte-ai/sdk@next @nyte-ai/host@next @nyte-ai/plugin@next
```

#### Run the host

This is a separate Node process, not code for Vite to bundle. It serves only the API on port 8787.

```ts title="chat-web/server.ts"
import process from "node:process";
import { sqliteStore } from "@nyte-ai/host";
import { chatOnlyProvider } from "@nyte-ai/host/providers";
import { sdk } from "@nyte-ai/sdk";

const store = sqliteStore({ path: "./agent.db" });
const host = await sdk.open({
  store,
  plugins: [{ id: "chat-only", environment: chatOnlyProvider() }],
  workspace: { kind: "chat-only", locator: null },
});

await host.models.setDefault({ provider: "openai-codex", id: "{{modelId}}" });

const listener = await host.listen({
  transport: { kind: "http", port: 8787 },
  auth: { kind: "token", token: process.env.NYTE_TOKEN ?? "" },
  origins: ["http://localhost:5173", "http://localhost:3000"],
});

console.log("Listening on", listener.address);

process.once("SIGINT", async () => {
  await host.close();
  await store.close();
});
```

`listen` binds `127.0.0.1` and refuses a token shorter than 16 characters. The host runs the
sessions it serves; `close()` closes its listeners first. Sign in against this store as in
[Make an API call](#make-an-api-call) before the first chat.

From `chat-web`, generate a host token and start the host:

```sh
export NYTE_TOKEN="$(node -e 'console.log(crypto.randomUUID())')"
printf '%s\n' "$NYTE_TOKEN"
node server.ts
```

#### Render the chat

Replace the generated `src/App.tsx`. Enter the token printed by the host to create a session.
`watch()` yields the whole view on every change, and resumes from where it stopped when the link
drops.

```tsx title="chat-web/src/App.tsx"
import { isPart, text } from "@nyte-ai/plugin/client";
import { sdk } from "@nyte-ai/sdk";
import type { Session, SessionView, UserContent } from "@nyte-ai/sdk";
import { useEffect, useState } from "react";

function contentText(content: UserContent) {
  return typeof content === "string"
    ? content
    : content.map((block) => (block.kind === "text" ? block.text : "")).join("");
}

export default function App() {
  const [token, setToken] = useState("");
  const [session, setSession] = useState<Session>();
  const [view, setView] = useState<SessionView>();
  const [input, setInput] = useState("");
  const [busy, setBusy] = useState(false);
  const [error, setError] = useState("");

  useEffect(() => {
    if (session === undefined) return;
    const views = session.watch()[Symbol.asyncIterator]();
    let open = true;

    void (async () => {
      for (let next = await views.next(); open && next.done !== true; next = await views.next())
        setView(next.value);
    })().catch((cause: unknown) => {
      if (open) setError(cause instanceof Error ? cause.message : String(cause));
    });

    return () => {
      open = false;
      void views.return?.();
    };
  }, [session]);

  async function submit() {
    setBusy(true);
    setError("");
    try {
      if (session === undefined) {
        const connection = await sdk.connect({
          url: "http://127.0.0.1:8787",
          credentials: { kind: "token", token },
        });
        setSession(await connection.sessions.create());
        return;
      }
      if (!input.trim()) return;
      await session.send(input, { delivery: "queue" });
      setInput("");
    } catch (cause) {
      setError(cause instanceof Error ? cause.message : String(cause));
    } finally {
      setBusy(false);
    }
  }

  const lastRun = view?.execution.kind === "idle" ? view.execution.lastRun : null;

  return (
    <main>
      <h1>Chat</h1>
      {view?.messages.map((message) =>
        message.kind === "user" ? (
          <p key={message.id} style={{ whiteSpace: "pre-wrap" }}>
            <strong>You: </strong>
            {contentText(message.content)}
            {message.status.kind === "landed" ? "" : ` (${message.status.kind})`}
          </p>
        ) : isPart(message, text) ? (
          <p key={message.id} style={{ whiteSpace: "pre-wrap" }}>
            <strong>AI: </strong>
            {message.state.markdown}
          </p>
        ) : null,
      )}
      {lastRun?.end.kind === "failed" && <p role="alert">{lastRun.end.failure.message}</p>}
      {error && <p role="alert">{error}</p>}
      <form
        onSubmit={(event) => {
          event.preventDefault();
          void submit();
        }}
      >
        {session === undefined ? (
          <label>
            Host token
            <input
              type="password"
              value={token}
              disabled={busy}
              onChange={(event) => setToken(event.target.value)}
              required
              minLength={16}
            />
          </label>
        ) : (
          <label>
            Message
            <input
              value={input}
              disabled={busy || view === undefined}
              onChange={(event) => setInput(event.target.value)}
              required
            />
          </label>
        )}
        <button disabled={busy || (session !== undefined && view === undefined)}>
          {session === undefined ? "Start chat" : "Send"}
        </button>
      </form>
    </main>
  );
}
```

In another terminal, from `chat-web`:

```sh
pnpm dev --host localhost --port 5173 --strictPort
```

Open `http://localhost:5173`. The host stores conversation history, so the browser sends only the
new message, not the whole transcript. This example creates a new session each time you start a
chat. Save `session.id` and reopen it with `connection.session(id)` after a reload.

A sent message is in `view.messages` at once, `unsent` until the host admits it, then `pending`
and `landed`. The sdk mints its id before the network and resends it under that id after a failed
request, so it lands once. This example leaves out tool rendering: every other part has a
`partKind`, a `state` and a `status` for a renderer to draw.

### Next.js

Keep the same host running. In a separate directory, create a standalone Next.js app, choose the
App Router without a `src` directory, and install the browser packages:

```sh
pnpm create next-app chat-next
cd chat-next
pnpm add @nyte-ai/sdk@next @nyte-ai/plugin@next
```

Copy the Vite `App.tsx` to `chat-next/app/page.tsx` and add `"use client";` before its imports.
Keep the generated root layout and Next config. The public release will ship compiled JavaScript
and type declarations, so it will not need `transpilePackages`.

```sh
pnpm dev --hostname localhost --port 3000
```

Open `http://localhost:3000` and enter the same host token. There is no Next.js API route in this
version. Both frontends call the same long-running host, which owns execution and storage. A
serverless request handler would not keep it running after the request ends. For that deployment
model, start with the
[Vercel template](https://github.com/interfaces-lab/nyte/blob/main/packages/host/src/deploy/vercel/README.md).

### Before deploying

The loopback URLs and token entry above are for local development. For a deployed frontend, use
an HTTPS host URL and allow its exact origin in `origins`. Never put provider credentials or a
shared host token in `VITE_*` or `NEXT_PUBLIC_*` variables; those values go into the browser
bundle. The token grants full access to this host, not just one session. For one principal per
device, mint a code with `host.principals.pair({ authority })` and connect with
`credentials: { kind: "pairing", code }`; the device token it yields is `connection.credential`.
Behind your own sign-in, `auth: { kind: "custom", authorize }` maps each request to a principal and
its authority. Nyte's SDK protocol is not the AI SDK UI message protocol, so `useChat` needs an
adapter rather than pointing directly at these endpoints.

## Make a TUI

Keep the host and render the session yourself. There is nothing to fold and nothing to retry:
`watch()` yields the view, and `send` journals the message before it reaches the wire.

```ts title="tui.ts"
import process from "node:process";
import { sdk } from "@nyte-ai/sdk";
import type { SessionView } from "@nyte-ai/sdk";

const connection = await sdk.connect({
  url: "http://127.0.0.1:8787",
  credentials: { kind: "token", token: process.env.NYTE_TOKEN ?? "" },
});
const session = await connection.sessions.create();

const draw = (view: SessionView) =>
  console.log(view.turns.length, "turns,", view.execution.kind, "execution");

await session.send("Explain this repository", { delivery: "queue" });

for await (const view of session.watch()) draw(view);
```

The sdk owns both directions. Reading, `watch()` resumes from its last position when the link
drops, so nothing is missed or repeated. Writing, `send` mints the message id, writes it to the
journal, and shows it `unsent`; on acknowledgement the entry is removed. If the client dies in
between, the next `connect` resends each entry under the same id, and the host admits it or
replays the receipt it already has.

`delivery: "steer"`, the default, joins the live run at its next boundary, and `"queue"` waits
for the current run to end; either starts a run when the head is idle. `"attach"` rides with the
next turn; a subagent's or background job's report also wakes a head whose last run completed,
but not one that was stopped or failed. The journal is in memory by default. For messages that
should survive a restart, pass `journal` to `connect`: an object with `load`, `put` and `remove`
over your own storage. To edit a message, `send(content, { replace: id })`.

## Or extend what's already there

To change what a client does, write a plugin. Core plugins from `@nyte-ai/plugin/core` add tools,
parts, commands, settings and hooks to sessions. Client plugins from `@nyte-ai/plugin/client` add
renderers, commands, settings, keybindings and client hooks; each declares the frameworks it
renders for, and the client mounts what it can. The supplied renderers are in
`@nyte-ai/plugin/renderers/react` and `@nyte-ai/plugin/renderers/tui`.

## What there is to copy

| Path                                  | What runs                                                       |
| ------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `packages/host/src/deploy/cloudflare` | One host in a SQLite-backed Durable Object, run from its alarm  |
| `packages/host/src/deploy/vercel`     | A Nitro app over PostgreSQL whose heads run as Vercel workflows |
| `packages/demo/website`               | Static interface previews, not a live agent                     |

The Cloudflare host is chat only, with no files or processes; the Vercel one runs tools in a
sandbox you supply. Setup is in the
[Cloudflare guide](https://github.com/interfaces-lab/nyte/blob/main/packages/host/src/deploy/cloudflare/README.md)
and the [Vercel guide](https://github.com/interfaces-lab/nyte/blob/main/packages/host/src/deploy/vercel/README.md).
